rules.quote: Find the responsible service or module in code and relevant repository instructions before adding a writer, listener, cache or poller.
rules.rule: Before adding a writer, listener, cache, or poller, find the responsible service or module in the code and the relevant repository instructions.

rules.quote: Extend or fix that owner.
rules.rule: Extend or fix the existing owner of shared behavior instead of adding a competing implementation.

rules.quote: Reuse behavior that differs only by data;
rules.rule: Reuse existing behavior when the variants differ only by data.

rules.quote: keep distinct locking, invariants or failure semantics separate.
rules.rule: Keep behaviors with distinct locking, invariants, or failure semantics separate rather than merging them.

rules.quote: Preserve the same authorization and safety gates across typed and raw entry points.
rules.rule: Apply the same authorization and safety gates across typed and raw entry points.

rules.quote: Passive config, health and telemetry paths must not bypass the command path.
rules.rule: Do not let passive config, health, or telemetry paths bypass the command path.

rules.quote: Reject unsupported changes explicitly
rules.rule: Reject unsupported changes explicitly rather than silently skipping them.

rules.quote: identify who corrects a detected fault; do not silently skip work or imply a diagnostic fixed it.
rules.rule: When a fault is detected, identify who corrects it, and do not imply that a diagnostic fixed it.

rules.quote: Resolve ownership conflicts explicitly rather than rewriting an invariant to hide a violation.
rules.rule: Resolve ownership conflicts explicitly rather than rewriting an invariant to hide a violation.

rules.quote: Use this check to guide ordinary work, not stall it.
rules.rule: Use the ownership check to guide ordinary work without stalling it.

rules.quote: Read the matching processes before acting, then use an exact verified PID or the PID saved at launch.
rules.rule: Before acting on processes, read the matching processes first, then act only on an exact verified PID or the PID saved at launch.

rules.quote: Never kill by pattern.
rules.rule: Never kill processes by pattern matching.

rules.quote: On hypervisors, routers, NAS or other shared hosts, use the owning platform's authorized actions instead of raw process signals.
rules.rule: On hypervisors, routers, NAS, or other shared hosts, use the owning platform's authorized actions instead of raw process signals.

rules.quote: Power-state restrictions still apply.
rules.rule: Follow power-state restrictions when managing shared hosts such as hypervisors, routers, or NAS devices.

rules.quote: For test cleanup, remove only the exact processes, sessions and files created by that test.
rules.rule: During test cleanup, remove only the exact processes, sessions, and files created by that test.

rules.quote: Inspect and verify the explicit target list before any destructive batch action.
rules.rule: Inspect and verify the explicit target list before performing any destructive batch action.

rules.quote: Never initiate shutdown, reboot, reset or power-cycle through shell, APIs, KVM, GPIO or another interface.
rules.rule: Never initiate a shutdown, reboot, reset, or power-cycle of a machine through any interface, including shell, APIs, KVM, GPIO, or others.

rules.quote: An exception requires the user to explicitly supersede this rule for the named power action and machine; generic recovery approval is insufficient.
rules.rule: Perform a power-state action (shutdown, reboot, reset, or power-cycle) on a machine only if the user explicitly supersedes the no-power-action rule for that named action and machine; generic recovery approval is not sufficient.

rules.quote: Do not automatically power a machine back on after requesting physical hardware work; its physical state may be unsafe.
rules.rule: Do not automatically power a machine back on after requesting physical hardware work.

rules.quote: Show a visible loading state until the first request settles.
rules.rule: Show a visible loading state in the interface until the first request settles.

rules.quote: Use an explicit first-settle flag, not merely `!loading`.
rules.rule: Track loading completion with an explicit first-settle flag rather than relying solely on the `!loading` condition.

rules.quote: Keep that flag sticky during refreshes
rules.rule: Keep the first-settle flag set once it has been set, so it stays true during subsequent refreshes.

rules.quote: so existing content does not flash back to a skeleton.
rules.rule: Do not show a skeleton loading state again during refreshes once existing content has loaded.

rules.quote: Disable controls while their underlying state is unknown;
rules.rule: Disable controls while their underlying state is unknown.

rules.quote: do not display unknown booleans as false
rules.rule: Do not display an unknown boolean value as false.

rules.quote: or unknown counts as zero.
rules.rule: Do not display an unknown count as zero.

rules.quote: Distinguish unavailable/error responses from successful empty results in both APIs and UI, with an explicit availability state and reason.
rules.rule: Distinguish unavailable or error responses from successful empty results in both APIs and the UI, using an explicit availability state and reason.

rules.quote: Settle the loading state on errors
rules.rule: Settle the loading state when a request results in an error.

rules.quote: and when no request will be made, such as a disabled feature or missing access.
rules.rule: Settle the loading state when no request will be made, such as for a disabled feature or missing access.

rules.quote: Verify that the loading indicator actually renders visibly.
rules.rule: Verify that the loading indicator actually renders visibly.

rules.quote: Do not change shared routing, firewall rules, DNS, reverse proxies or port bindings as a workaround for an application problem.
rules.rule: Do not change shared routing, firewall rules, DNS, reverse proxies, or port bindings as a workaround for an application problem.

rules.quote: Inspect the owning configuration and logs to identify the actual fault
rules.rule: Inspect the owning configuration and logs to identify the actual fault before making changes.

rules.quote: do not prescribe a blanket service restart
rules.rule: Do not prescribe a blanket service restart as a fix.

rules.quote: A necessary shared-state change requires explicit authorization for that change and its affected services, with the impact explained beforehand.
rules.rule: Make a necessary shared-state change only with explicit authorization for that specific change and its affected services, explaining the impact beforehand.

rules.quote:
Do not keep
recommending pairing after this preference is stated.
rules.rule: Do not recommend pairing codes, pairing links, or QR pairing as a sign-in solution once the user has stated this preference.

rules.quote:
prefer the existing Authentik identity with normal
browser sign-in and automatic credential renewal across desktop, web, and mobile.
rules.rule: For self-hosted applications, prefer sign-in through the existing Authentik identity using normal browser sign-in with automatic credential renewal across desktop, web, and mobile.

rules.quote:
eliminating manual codes is not
permission to disable authentication or create permanent shared credentials.
rules.rule: Do not disable authentication or create permanent shared credentials when eliminating manual pairing codes for self-hosted applications.

rules.quote:
Reuse existing service
owners and preserve running fleet sessions.
rules.rule: For T3 self-hosting work, reuse existing service owners and preserve running fleet sessions.

rules.quote:
Necessary authentication changes or
maintained patches are preferable to a pairing-code workaround.
rules.rule: For T3, prefer necessary authentication changes or maintained patches over a pairing-code workaround.
